findings.message: `jsonLines` drops every timeline line that does not parse, and says nothing. `lessons()` and `openSpan()` both build on it, so a corrupt record reads the same as no record. The README promises the opposite: "A record that does not parse is counted, never guessed at." Today a broken lesson line just disappears from the lesson count, and a broken `stop` line leaves its span drawn as still running. Fix: count the unparsed timeline lines per change. Show that count in the LEARNING section and on the build row, the way TOKENS shows its unreadable records, or draw the section as an error. Add a table test over three cases: a truncated lesson line, a truncated stop line, and a non-object JSON line.
findings.scenario: A timeline.jsonl holds two lesson lines; the second is cut short (`{"kind":"lesson","at":"2026-11-14T06:00`). The pane shows `1 lessons · pattern 1` with no unreadable note. In a second case, `{"ev":"start","span":"W1",...}` is followed by a truncated `{"ev":"stop","span":"W1` line. The build row shows `wave 1 5h 12m` as if the wave were still running.

findings.message: The prefilter skips any line that contains neither `"usage":{` nor `Title":` before trying to parse it. A corrupt assistant record that was cut off before its usage block is therefore never added to `unreadable`. Its spend is lost and the totals still print without `≥`. Fix: count a line as unreadable when it fails to parse and mentions `"type":"assistant"`, or when it does not end in `}`.

`refresh` runs from `tool.call`, `turn.complete` and `command.run`, and these can overlap. Each run writes its result with `update($, view, () => next)`, so whichever run finishes last wins. A run that started earlier but finishes later overwrites a newer view with older data until the next refresh. Fix: drop the result when `next.at` is older than the stored view's `at`, or chain refreshes so they run one at a time.

`atHead` compares prefixes in both directions and sets no minimum length. A round file whose `head` is very short, such as `"a"` or `"ab"`, matches any HEAD that starts with those characters and is drawn as `at HEAD`. Fix: require at least 7 hex characters before comparing, and treat anything shorter as unknown.

`summarize` keeps only the top 5 roles, through `top(..., n)`, and the pane gives no sign that any were cut. With more than 5 agent roles, the `by role:` line silently leaves out the rest of the spend. Fix: add an `· others $x` entry for the roles beyond the top 5, or say how many were left out.
